description: Igneus is a multidisciplinary team from San Luis, Argentina, bringing together a chemical engineer, a full-stack developer, and four high school students. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS active fire data, making fire activity easier to explore and helping identify historical patterns and critical periods. From San Luis to the world, we turn science, technology, and collaboration into action.
summary: IGNEUS transforms 26 years (2000–2026) of raw NASA MODIS and VIIRS thermal data into a clean, harmonized time series for Argentina, with a globally scalable architecture. By deduplicating simultaneous satellite passes on a ~1 km grid, we consolidated over 6.4M raw records into 3.4M representative detections. Our interactive web app integrates spatial filters, seasonal patterns, AI assistance, Copernicus CAMS GFAS carbon emissions (CO₂, CO, CH₄), El Niño/La Niña (ENSO) climate correlations, and proximity alerts—empowering authorities and communities to shift from reactive firefighting to prevention.
details:
What exactly does IGNEUS do?

IGNEUS is an open-science web platform that organizes, harmonizes, and visualizes 26 years (November 1, 2000 – November 15, 2026) of satellite thermal detections across Argentina using NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS). It integrates Copernicus CAMS GFAS wildfire carbon emissions (2003–2026), NOAA El Niño/La Niña (ONI) climate indices, and official provincial boundaries from Argentina's API Georef.

Designed for national-scale analysis with San Luis Province as a deep-dive case study, the public application (https://igneus.streamlit.app/) features 12 interactive views:

  • AI Assistant
  • Map
  • Calendar
  • Harmonization
  • Charts
  • El Niño / La Niña
  • Carbon Emissions
  • Near Me
  • Origin (Inferred)
  • Agricultural / Prescribed Burns
  • Method & Sources
  • Data

Throughout the interface, IGNEUS enforces strict scientific transparency: a satellite thermal detection is not a confirmed wildfire, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP, in MW) measures estimated radiative energy output—not burned area, total fire intensity, or operational risk.

How does it work?

  • 1. Data Ingestion & Sensor Coverage: The historical series (2000–2025) was built from NASA FIRMS Archive (Standard Processing) scientific files across 48 annual/sensor files, fully incorporating all 26 years including MODIS 2005 (69,750 records), 2010 (61,838 records), and 2016 (54,982 records). The preliminary 2026 segment (January 1 – November 15, 2026) combines FIRMS Archive and Near Real-Time (NRT) feeds. Covered instruments include MODIS Terra (since Nov 1, 2000), MODIS Aqua (since Jul 4, 2002), VIIRS Suomi-NPP (since Jan 20, 2012), VIIRS NOAA-20 (since 2018), and VIIRS NOAA-21 (recent period). All records were consolidated into a unified Apache Parquet master dataset of 6,444,727 rows and 16 columns.
  • 2. Period Separation & Instrumental Outage Documentation:
    • Historical Baseline (2000–2025): Filtered to presumed vegetation fires (type == 0), yielding 6,154,332 raw detections and 3,297,501 deduplicated representative events.
    • Preliminary 2026 (Jan 1 – Nov 15, 2026): Combines Archive and NRT feeds (290,395 raw detections; 126,397 representative events). Because NRT feeds lack the land-cover classification field (type), 2026 represents a broader thermal anomaly universe and is explicitly separated from direct historical comparisons.
    • MODIS Terra 2001 Outage: Documents an instrumental gap from June 15 to July 3, 2001 (Julian days 166–184), cross-verified against official NASA MODAPS/MCST logs confirming Terra MODIS entered Survival/Safe Mode. This reflects sensor availability rather than absence of fire activity.
  • 3. Spatiotemporal Deduplication & Cross-Sensor Harmonization: To prevent multi-satellite double counting, IGNEUS applies a deterministic calendar-day spatial grid of 0.01° × 0.01° (~1.11 km north-south), ranking simultaneous detections by standardized confidence (High > Nominal > Low) and descending FRP to flag redundant records (es_duplicado) while preserving 100% of raw detections for side-by-side comparison. During the multi-sensor overlap period (2012–2025, MODIS + VIIRS), 52.6% of raw vegetation detections are flagged as redundant. IGNEUS also computes a Suomi-NPP equivalent time series using provincial-monthly calibration factors (median relative error of 7.3% nationally and 12.0% provincially, compared to 126–127% for uncalibrated multi-sensor sums).
  • 4. Territorial Reconciliation & San Luis Case Study:
    • National Master vs. Deployed Georef Universe: The master Parquet covers Argentina's bounding box (6,444,727 raw / 3,423,898 representative detections). Inside the deployed Streamlit app, spatial filtering against Argentina's 24 official provincial polygons (API Georef v2.0) yields 6,433,645 unique detections and 3,416,956 representative events (excluding 11,082 raw / 6,942 representative offshore or border-outside points, and accounting for 591 shared boundary points across 23 provincial pairs).
    • San Luis Case Study: Within the San Luis audit bounding box (-36.0° to -31.8° lat, -67.3° to -64.7° lon), 2000–2025 comprises 179,778 raw and 80,131 representative detections. During the severe September 29, 2020 event, IGNEUS consolidates 3,130 raw detections into 547 representative events (peak FRP: 2,086.2 MW recorded by MODIS Aqua at 06:21 UTC). Under the official Georef provincial polygon in the app, San Luis records 1,904 representative events in September 2020 and 1,926 in October 2020.
  • 5. Independent Carbon Emissions Module (Copernicus CAMS GFAS, 2003–2026): The Carbon Emissions view integrates daily gridded biomass burning fluxes (0.1° × 0.1° resolution, 1,576,326 active grid-day records from Jan 2, 2003 to Nov 11, 2026) from ECMWF CAMS GFAS (products v1.2 and v1.4.2). Fluxes (co2fire, cofire, ch4fire, cfire in kg m⁻² s⁻¹) are integrated into metric tons per cell-day using exact spherical cell area and packaged into lightweight monthly (287 rows) and annual-spatial (264,005 cell-year rows) Parquet tables. Cumulative modeled emissions across Argentina (2003–2026) total:
    • CO₂: 3,727.78 Mt
    • CO: 163.57 Mt
    • CH₄: 7.13 Mt
    • Total Carbon (C): 1,102.41 Mt
    • (These are model-derived atmospheric flux estimates and remain strictly separate from FIRMS hotspot counts).
  • 6. Statistical FRP Benchmark & Independent Audit: Across the 3,297,501 historical representative detections (2000–2025), 3,297,186 have positive FRP (99.9904%; 315 zero-FRP records; zero nulls or negatives), showing a right-skewed distribution: mean 31.29 MW, median 9.60 MW, 90th percentile 60.70 MW, 99th percentile 369.50 MW, and maximum 13,294.50 MW. An independent audit in Google Colab verified schema integrity, reproduced the national API Georef spatial join across all 24 jurisdictions with zero discrepancy (6,433,645 raw / 3,416,956 unique), and independently reconstructed historical deduplication across all 6,154,332 records with 99.8385% record-level agreement (6,144,392 exact matches; 9,940 edge cases traced to pre-type-filtering tie-breaking).

What are the benefits?

  • Scientific Rigor & Reproducibility: Eliminates multi-sensor inflation through an explicit, auditable spatiotemporal rule, documented satellite outages, and separated data universes.
  • Environmental & Territorial Intelligence: Transforms 6.44 million fragmented satellite records into an accessible public tool linking fire regimes, ENSO climate phases, and carbon emissions.
  • Replicability: The modular Parquet pipeline and 0.01° deduplication framework can be replicated for any country or region covered by NASA FIRMS.

Expected Impact & Intended Use

IGNEUS provides researchers, educators, environmental agencies, civil protection planners, and land managers with an open-science benchmark to explore historical fire recurrence, seasonal peaks, and climate-fire teleconnections across Argentina. IGNEUS is an exploratory historical and analytical platform; it does not replace real-time operational fire-weather warning systems or ground-based emergency dispatch.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Data Engineering & Auditing: Python, Pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, GeoPandas (EPSG:4326), Apache Parquet, Google Colab.
  • Web Application & Visualization: Streamlit, Plotly, Mapbox.
  • Climate & Geographic Reference Data: NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ONI, ± 0.5 °C Niño 3.4 threshold), Argentina API Georef v2.0, Copernicus CAMS GFAS.
  • AI Integration & Development Support: Google Gemini (gemini-3.6-flash powering the context-aware AI Assistant inside Streamlit; plus technical scripting and translation support) and Anthropic Claude (methodological audit design and consistency review).

Known Limitations

  • A thermal anomaly does not confirm an active wildfire, and FRP does not measure burned area or fire severity.
  • The 2026 NRT/Archive segment lacks the FIRMS land-cover type field and is not directly comparable to the type == 0 historical baseline (2000–2025).
  • Sub-provincial San Luis audit figures use a rectangular bounding box, whereas the Streamlit provincial filter uses the official API Georef polygon.
  • Satellite availability in the S-NPP harmonization module is inferred from observed detections rather than orbital swath coverage logs, and cross-sensor calibration is empirically validated for Aqua-to-S-NPP (with additional uncertainty for Terra and NOAA-20/21).
  • In the CAMS GFAS monthly summary metadata, the batch version string labels all of 2025 as v1.2 even though operational ADS transition to v1.4/v1.4.2 occurred during 2025; underlying emission values are verified and unaffected.
  • Full execution of the 20-point end-to-end Streamlit UI test checklist remains scheduled as post-hackathon quality assurance.
